title: Young talents who could shine in the Premier League in 2026
seoTitle: Young talents poised to shine in the Premier League 2026
subtitle: Discover who could become a protagonist in the 20 English top-flight clubs
excerpt: On August 4, 2026, the Premier League kicks off the season with 20 young players, one from each club, ready to make their mark and surprise.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 4, 2026, the Premier League opens its season with a list of 20 youngsters, one from each club, who are looking to cement their place in the squads. The expectation is that some of these athletes will become key players throughout the campaign.

Arsenal: Max Dowman emerges

The 16-year-old striker who broke the record as the youngest Premier League scorer last season returns to Arsenal with the mission of being more than a reserve. He made six league appearances and scored in a friendly against Girona, demonstrating versatility both on the wing and as a number 10. Manager Mikel Arteta is still protecting the youngster, but the season could bring more regular opportunities.

Bournemouth: Veljko Milosavljevic seeks recovery

The 19-year-old centre-back, already a Serbian international, became the youngest Bournemouth player to start a Premier League match when he faced Brighton. He featured in seven games in the 2025-26 campaign, with four wins and a draw. A knee injury has kept him out of action since January, but he aims to resume the strong start he had at the Vitality Stadium.

Brighton: Zadok Yohanna arrives with expectations

The 19-year-old Nigerian right-winger was signed for £21.5 million from AIK of Stockholm, where he scored five goals and provided four assists in 18 matches. Former midfielder Warren Aspinall commented that the signing prevented clubs like Chelsea and Newcastle from moving ahead, adding: "It's a little bit of a scalp because two other big clubs in England were chasing him in Chelsea and Newcastle , so they got ahead of them which is very good,". "Have we got another diamond to polish up? That's what we are looking for - these rough diamonds to polish up and sell on for big money."

Chelsea: Dastan Satpaev could be a revelation

The 17-year-old Kazakhstani striker has been identified as the prospect most likely to break into the first team. He has received praise from manager Xabi Alonso and already scored in the match against Western Sydney Wanderers. He has Champions League experience and has earned nine caps for the national team since 2025.

Manchester United: Shea Lacey gains ground

The youngster who reached the fringes of the first team at the end of Ruben Amorim's tenure stood out by scoring a hat-trick in the youth categories and influencing the match against Atlético de Madrid in Stockholm, winning the penalty that Bryan Mbeumo converted. The trend is that he will be used as a substitute, starting games on the right side and moving inward.

Other names worth watching

Among the other young players mentioned are midfielder Kai Andrews, who debuted for the Sky Blues at 17 and has already worn the Wales national team shirt; striker Jonah Kusi-Asare, who joined Fulham for £5 million and could see more minutes with the departure of Raúl Jiménez; and full-back Ryan McAidoo, who scored on his FA Cup debut and impressed manager Enzo Maresca. Each of these athletes has the chance to turn promise into regular performance over the campaign.

With information from BBC Sport.
